articles.title: Check your iOS app's App Store rank in 155 countries with Python (free)
articles.excerpt: If you ship an iOS app, App Store Connect tells you downloads and revenue, but not where your app sits in the top charts of each country. That number matters more than it looks. A jump from #80 to #30…
articles.body: If you ship an iOS app, App Store Connect tells you downloads and revenue, but not where your app sits in the top charts of each country. That number matters more than it looks. A jump from #80 to #30 in the Travel chart in Germany usually means a feature, a review, or a competitor slipping, and you want to know the day it happens, not a month later. I built a small free tool for this, and in this post I show both ways: the do-it-yourself script against Apple's own feed, and the shortcut. Why the usual approach hurts Apple publishes the top charts as a public RSS/JSON feed, one URL per country, per chart (free, paid, grossing) and per genre. That is the honest source, and you can use it yourself.
articles.author: Martin Petrov

articles.title: JSON Compress, lossless JSON compression whose output is still JSON
articles.excerpt: First published on the Tech Style blog. Send a thousand records over an API and you send a thousand copies of every key name. A status with four possible values is spelled out a thousand times, and so…
articles.body: First published on the Tech Style blog . Send a thousand records over an API and you send a thousand copies of every key name. A status with four possible values is spelled out a thousand times, and so is a currency that is always "GBP". Minifying takes out the whitespace, which is the small part of the problem. The repetition stays. JSON Compress is our open-source library for the repetition. It writes each key name once, turns arrays of like-shaped objects into columns and rows, and stores repeated values once. On record-shaped data the result is typically 45 to 75% smaller than minified JSON, and it comes back byte for byte. The output is still JSON, so it goes wherever the original went: an HTTP body, a WebSocket frame, a Postgres jsonb column, a queue message.

articles.title: Your Free 10M Tokens Should Buy Failures, Not Features
articles.excerpt: Free tokens are not a discount. They are a single grant. You spend them once, and you cannot spend them again. My position: spend a free token grant on the harness, not on the product. A demo proves t…
articles.body: Free tokens are not a discount. They are a single grant. You spend them once, and you cannot spend them again. My position: spend a free token grant on the harness, not on the product. A demo proves the model can answer once. A harness tells you how often it fails. Only one of those survives contact with users. The claim, stated plainly A fixed free grant is a measurement budget. It is not seed capital for features. If you burn it on a chat UI, you learn nothing you can reuse. If you burn it on failure data, you keep the data after the grant expires. MonkeyCode is relevant here because the operator advertises two things that fit this argument: free model access and a free server option. Treat both as availability claims, not as guarantees.

articles.title: From policy PDF to runtime: enforcing AI governance on every agent call
articles.excerpt: There's a gap between having an AI usage policy and enforcing it. The document says "the support agent doesn't access financial data". But who guarantees that on call #4,385, at 2 a.m., when nobody is…
articles.body: There's a gap between having an AI usage policy and enforcing it. The document says "the support agent doesn't access financial data". But who guarantees that on call #4,385, at 2 a.m., when nobody is watching? Governance that lives in a PDF is intent. Governance that lives in the runtime is operations. What a contextual policy (CSP) is A Contextual Security Policy ties a permission decision to the context of the execution, not just to the identity of the caller. Five axes cover most real-world needs: Origin — which channel or application the request came from. Schedule — time windows in which certain actions are allowed. Data — which fields the agent can read or write. Behavior — limits on volume, frequency and escalation. Custom — rules specific to your domain.

articles.body: Weather apps are designed to be opened, used, and closed. A session. The mental model is: I need weather → open app → check → close app. The alternative model: weather is ambient information that is simply visible when you open a browser tab. No session, no navigation, no intent required. Weather and Clock Dashboard for Firefox Puts current weather conditions and a live clock on your Firefox new tab. Every time you open a new tab: Current temperature (Celsius or Fahrenheit, your choice) Current conditions (sunny, cloudy, rain, etc.) An analog clock showing the current time Nothing else. No forecast cards, no UV index, no radar. Just the current state.

articles.title: Attacker Rides Qubole's Trusted AWS Account Into Customer Environments, Steals Secrets and S3 Data
articles.excerpt: TL;DR what: An attacker used credentials for Qubole's own AWS account (805246085872) to assume vendor IAM roles in multiple customer AWS accounts from October 14 to October 26. impact: The attacker pu…
articles.body: TL;DR what: An attacker used credentials for Qubole's own AWS account (805246085872) to assume vendor IAM roles in multiple customer AWS accounts from October 14 to October 26. impact: The attacker pulled secrets from Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store, validated AWS, Entra ID and Okta credentials with TruffleHog, and copied S3 data, sometimes entire buckets. fix: Wiz advises rotating everything a compromised Qubole role could reach, revoking active sessions, removing unused Qubole roles, and restricting vendor trust policies by source IP or VPC endpoint; Qubole and its owner Idera had not published a statement at the time of writing.

articles.body: 当去年的作业，一次提示就能完成 Mihail Eric 在斯坦福教授《现代软件开发者》课程 CS146S，同时负责 Monaco 的 AI 工作。这两种角色让他能够同时观察：学生如何学习 AI 编程，以及工程团队如何使用编程智能体。 CS146S 首次开课时设置了九次作业和一个综合项目。其中一项练习要求学生在代码仓库上运行 AI 代码审查工具，并评估工具给出的反馈。 到下一轮开课时，Eric 判断，许多练习已经可以由智能体通过一次提示完成。他曾询问一群斯坦福大二、大三学生如何编程，受询学生都已在使用智能体。 这让课程面临一个具体问题： 如果生成代码不再足以体现学习成果，作业还应该考查什么？ 从课堂练习，转向真实的开源贡献 新一轮课程将部分作业调整为向开源项目贡献代码，由项目维护者审查学生提交的补丁。 与封闭的课堂练习相比，这类任务增加了几项不能仅靠生成代码解决的要求： 确认维护者是否真的需要这项功能； 理解现有代码为什么这样运行； 判断补丁可能影响哪些其他行为； 根据维护者的反馈解释、修改和完善方案。 智能体可以在一个下午实现功能，但功能是否适合进入项目，仍需要沟通与判断。学生也因此获得了向资深开发者学习的机会。 这里的变化，不只是把作业放进公开仓库，而是让学习成果接受真实项目需求与维护标准的检验。 能提交补丁，不等于能解释补丁 讨论中还介绍了 Geoffrey Litt 的 explain-diff 技能：它会将代码变更转化为可视化讲解，再围绕变更向使用者提问。 一个可以直接尝试的练习是：把智能体刚写好的补丁交给它，看看哪些问题会让自己不得不重新打开代码。 这也提出了一个适合在 写好标智库 展开讨论的工程实践问题：当代码生成越来越容易，开发者该如何检验自己是否真正理解了改动？ 能够提交补丁，与能够解释补丁，并不是同一件事。 这类练习将注意力从“代码是否生成了”，转向“开发…

articles.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
articles.excerpt: New research suggests that Little Red Dots, which have puzzled astronomers since the JWST began discovering them, could host primordial black holes born during the Big Bang.
articles.body: Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium.

articles.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
articles.excerpt: Starfish Space's first Otter servicing spacecraft suffered a glitch in orbit recently, ending its technology-demonstrating mission for NASA.
articles.body: Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short.

articles.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
articles.excerpt: NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there is $1 million in prizes for the best ideas.
articles.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said.

articles.title: NASA needs more astronauts for moon missions and beyond. You can apply now, but only until Dec. 3
articles.excerpt: On Saturday (Nov. 7), NASA put out the call for applications for a new class of astronauts. Applications are due by Dec. 3.
articles.body: If NASA ever hopes to build a permanent moon base for astronauts, let alone aim for Mars, the U.S. space agency is going to need a whole lot of space travelers. And now, you have a chance to be one of them. NASA on Saturday (Nov. 7) put out the call for a new class of astronaut candidates who think they have the "right stuff" to fly, live and work in space. Those astronaut hopefuls have until Dec. 3 to apply ( the application website is here ), with NASA planning to make its final selections in late 2027. "This is an extraordinary time to join NASA's astronaut corps," the space agency's chief, Jared Isaacman, said in an announcement , which was made during NASA's "Max Power" air show at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida.
